old_title: Iran war live: US fires on ship for defying blockade as Trump claims Hormuz control
new_title: Iran war live: Tehran threatens to prolong war until Trump's term ends
old_text:
The US military fired on a Panamanian-flagged ship in the Gulf of Oman yesterday after accusing it of trying to evade the American blockade on Iranian ports.
The military said the vessel had ignored warnings to stop, prompting an American helicopter to fire missiles into the engine room of the M/V Vela Nova, disabling the ship.
Details of the incident emerged as the US president told reporters late on Tuesday night that "we totally control the Strait of Hormuz ... Nobody else, only us". "At some point, maybe they'll do something and then they get blown away," he added of Iran.
Iran was resolute on Tuesday it continued to exert power over the strait, and that the US must end the war before they will allow normal shipping to be restored.
Mohsen Rezaee, the new secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, said on social media that the "message is clear" that the strait will remain shut until the US agrees to terms and pulls back.
Earlier this week, Trump snubbed Iran's six conditions for reopening the strait, which included "payment in full" for damage inflicted on Iran throughout the war.
Just 29% of expected midterm voters say they approve of Trump's handling of Iran
A cable TV polling expert claims that numbers from two surveys conducted two years apart show just how deeply President Donald Trump has disappointed America's voters when it comes to Iran.
CNN chief data analyst Harry Enten said Tuesday that a July 2024 poll of people who were extremely motivated to vote in that year's presidential election found that 53 percent were confident Trump would be able to handle the situation in Iran, according to a video clip posted online.
But a July poll of people extremely motivated to vote in November's midterm elections shows that just 29 percent now approve of how Trump is actually handling Iran, Enten said.
"We're talking about a 24-point fall in just two years," he said. "What was an advantage for President Trump going into the 2024 election amongst those who really wanted to turn out and vote has turned into a tremendous disadvantage this time around."
Iranian-backed Houthis kill 6 in attack on vessel
At least six people were killed by Iran-backed Houthi rebels attacking a vessel in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, the Yemeni authorities said.
Yemen's coast guard said the dead included four crew members and two members of the government-allied National Resistance Forces.
Houthis fired three ballistic missiles at the Yemeni commercial vessel, according to Yemen's internationally recognised government.
They are the first known deaths from Houthi attacks on shipping off Yemen in the latest bout of fighting in the Arab country.
Drones hit Iranian Kurdish opposition camps
Four drones hit three Iranian Kurdish opposition camps near Erbil in Iraq this morning, with no casualties reported, security sources told Reuters.
Pakistan says three sailors killed in Red Sea attack
At least three Pakistani nationals were killed in an attack on a ship in the Red Sea, the foreign ministry said.
"Pakistan strongly condemns the Houthi attack on a non-combatant commercial vessel," the foreign minister said on X.
The alleged attack comes as Iran-backed Houthis have been accused of increasing attacks on vessels near the waters of Yemen.
Syria says IAEA will announce 'significant progress' on nuclear file
Syria will host a delegation from the International Atomic Energy Agency in the coming days to announce "significant progress" on the issue of nuclear materials, Syria's Atomic Energy Commission said.
Since the ouster of president Bashar al-Assad in late 2024, Syria's new authorities have committed to working with the United Nations' nuclear watchdog to address the legacy of nuclear activities during decades of Assad family rule
Israeli military 'mistakenly' launches interceptor in Lebanon
The Israeli army said an interceptor was mistakenly launched in Southern Lebanon this morning.
The Israeli Defense Forces (IDF) said the interceptor had been launched at a target that was later confirmed to be IDF fire from operations carried out within the Security Zone.
Trump demands reparations from Iran for 'all the people they have killed'
President Donald Trump is demanding that Iran pay compensation to American victims of Iranian-backed attacks as he responds to Tehran's own demand for war reparations.
In a Monday post on Truth Social, Trump said he had "instructed my representatives to put this firmly into any, and all, future negotiations" - casting Iran's compensation demand as a novel idea he was happy to borrow.
More here.
US ambassador claims Iranian regime weakest since 1979
The US ambassador to Israel has claimed that the Iranian regime is the "weakest they have been since they took over in 1979" amid Donald Trump's war on Tehran.
"The operation between the United States and Israel did an enormous level of damage," Mike Huckabee told Newsmax, praising the US president's bid to "bankrupt them".
US fires on ship it said was trying to break blockade of Iran
The US military said that its forces fired on a Panamanian-flagged ship in the Gulf of Oman that tried to evade the American blockade on Iranian ports. The move came as president Donald Trump tries to keep economic pressure on the Islamic Republic.
US Central Command said the vessel had ignored warnings to stop, prompting an American helicopter to fire missiles into the engine room of the M/V Vela Nova, disabling the ship.
The statement did not say whether the ship's crew suffered any casualties.
new_text:
Iran has suggested it could deliberately prolong the war with the US until Donald Trump leaves office, in order to send a message that attacking the country has lasting consequences.
Mohammad Reza Naghdi, senior adviser to the commander of Iran's Revolutionary Guards, said dragging out the war would show any future US administration that "there is a cost" to hostile endeavours against Iran.
"We have to attain deterrence so that the enemy never dares to attack us, so we can live with security," he told PBS NewsHour.
His comments came as Iran again rejected Donald Trump's claims that the US has "total control" over the Strait of Hormuz.
Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority said "the Strait of Hormuz remains blocked" and it will not be opened until Iran's conditions are accepted.
Trump earlier said that "praise be to Allah", Washington has "total control over the Strait of Hormuz", adding: "I THINK WE WILL KEEP IT!"
Amid their conflicting claims, data from trade intelligence firm Kpler showed shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz was near a three-month low.
Just 13 vessels transited the waterway on Tuesday, around 90 per cent below the pre-war daily average.
Iran says it could prolong war until Trump leaves office
A senior adviser to the commander of Iran's Revolutionary Guards said Tehran could deliberately prolong the war until US President Donald Trump leaves office, in an effort to wear down its adversaries and deter future attacks.
Mohammad Reza Naghdi told PBS NewsHour that extending the conflict could impose a cost on any future US administration considering military action against Iran.
"We have to attain deterrence so that the enemy never dares to attack us, so we can live with security," he said.
Naghdi also defended Iranian attacks on civilian vessels attempting to cross the Strait of Hormuz, saying Tehran needed to control shipping routes during wartime.
He said vessels passing through areas controlled by Iran could be viewed as a threat if they were suspected of carrying supplies for the enemy.
"When we are at war, vessels need to pass through a region we can control," he said. "When they leave an area that we control, it could be that they're transporting supplies for the enemy."
Asked whether attacking civilian ships violated international law, Naghdi said Iran had the right to control routes it considered threatening during a war.
US forces confirm continued blockade in Hormuz
US Central Command said its forces have redirected 59 commercial vessels, disabled three and boarded two as part of enforcement of its "steel wall blockade" against Iran.
The latest update comes as shipping traffic remains low through the Strait of Hormuz, with both sides continuing to make contradictory claims over control of the waterway.
Centcom said the figures were as of Wednesday as an F/A-18 fighter jet launched from the USS George HW Bush in regional waters.
UK economy grew by 0.4% in second quarter as Iran war prompts slowdown
Economic growth in the UK slowed between April and June, as the fallout from Donald Trump's war on Iran put strain on global finances.
The UK economy grew by 0.4 per cent in the second quarter of the year, according to the Office for National Statistics, down from 0.6 per cent in the first quarter.
Its data showed growth of 0.3 per cent month-on-month in June, against expectations for a flat performance, as the ONS said firms across the service sector reported buoyant trade thanks to extreme hot weather and the start of the World Cup football tournament.
Desperate US sailors trying to jump overboard on extended Middle East deployment, families say
Desperate sailors aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln have tried to jump overboard during an extended deployment in the Middle East, their families say.
The aircraft carrier, crewed by around 5,000 sailors and Marines, has been deployed since November 21 but more lately has been supporting U.S. military operations in the war with Iran. The deployment had been expected to end in May but has been extended with no current return date, families told The Military Times.
Annabelle Loma, the wife of a sailor serving on the Abraham Lincoln, told the publication her husband is now on medical hold after trying to jump from the carrier.
ICJP calls on UK to sanction trade with Israeli settlements
The International Centre of Justice for Palestinians (ICJP) has written to Middle East minister Stephen Doughty calling on the UK government to impose targeted sanctions on trade with Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank.
The group said Doughty's recent condemnation of settlement expansion must be accompanied by "concrete measures", arguing that sanctions are needed to bring the UK in line with its obligations under international law.
ICJP pointed to Israel's approval of plans for 13 new settlements in the West Bank and more than £300m in funding announced for settlement construction as evidence of an accelerating expansion of the settlement enterprise.
The group also cited growing calls within the UK for action, including a June letter signed by 140 Labour MPs urging a ban on trade with Israeli settlements.
Órlaith Roe, ICJP's public affairs and communications officer, said sanctions were "the bare minimum" required to uphold international law and urged Doughty to act without delay.
US gas prices hit their highest mark ever for mid August as Trump's Iran war drags on
US gas prices on Wednesday hit their highest-ever price for this point in the year, according to GasBuddy.
Patrick De Haan, the head of petroleum analysis at GasBuddy, reported in a post on X that gas prices have never gone above $4 per gallon after August 12 in any year.
On Wednesday morning, the average fuel price was just over $4 per gallon. The last time fuel cost nearly that much around mid-August was in 2022, when the national average gas price was $3.98 per gallon.

X suspends Houthi spokesman's account
X has suspended the account of Yahya Saree, the military spokesman for Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels.
The account, which had more than 121,000 followers, now displays a notice saying it was suspended for violating the platform's rules.
Saree regularly used it to announce Houthi attacks on ships in the Red Sea, as well as operations targeting Saudi Arabia and Yemen's internationally recognised government.
Iran says 'no talk of an extension' of 60 day ceasefire
Iran and the United States remain at loggerheads over efforts to agree a permanent end to the war in the Gulf, according to a senior Iranian source who said there had been no progress in talks to revive the interim deal agreed in June and define a timeframe to implement it.
The comments were a further blow to hopes of a swift resolution to the crisis, following attacks on shipping in the region on Tuesday that pushed oil prices higher.
"One of the issues that is being discussed via mediators is the US returning to the interim agreement and defining a timeframe for implementing the commitments. There has been absolutely no progress on this issue," the Iranian source said.
The Iranian source dismissed a report on Wednesday from Turkey's Anadolu news agency that quoted Pakistani government sources as saying they had agreed to extend that 60-day period.
"There is no talk of an extension because, from Iran's perspective, there is no period that began and therefore nothing to extend. The United States violated the interim agreement 48 hours after it was reached and withdrew from it a few days later," the source told Reuters.
Both Iran and the United States have stepped up rhetoric in the past two days.
Iran's top security official, Mohsen Rezaei, said on Tuesday that the Strait of Hormuz would remain closed unless the US accepted Iran's conditions to end the war.
That followed a new demand from Trump on Monday that Iran should pay compensation for people killed in 50 years of wars, attacks and protests.
Trump defends secret flight swap after using Air Force One as decoy: 'The plane I flew on was at greater risk'
President Donald Trump has defended a ruse that saw him stow away in an airport catering container to slip into another plane while Air Force One, filled with staff, and reporters, essentially worked as an unwitting decoy.
Trump was sent into the sky out of Turkey in the second plane after a recent summit in Turkey because the Secret Service and military wanted him on a "different plane" due to a threat from Iran.
"I think actually the plane that I flew on was at greater risk," Trump told reporters on Tuesday. "I think it was at greater risk because that would be the plane I think that they would be more likely to go for."
Trump's Iran approval plunges 24 points among voters
A cable TV polling expert claims that numbers from two surveys conducted two years apart show just how deeply President Donald Trump has disappointed America's voters when it comes to Iran.
CNN chief data analyst Harry Enten said Tuesday that a July 2024 poll of people who were extremely motivated to vote in that year's presidential election found that 53 percent were confident Trump would be able to handle the situation in Iran, according to a video clip posted online.
But a July poll of people extremely motivated to vote in November's midterm elections shows that just 29 percent now approve of how Trump is actually handling Iran, Enten said.
